title: Concord NC Homes: Styles, Neighborhoods & What to Expect
label: Concord Homes
metaDescription: What homes in Concord NC actually look like — styles, ages, lot sizes, and price tiers across the city's neighborhoods, explained by a local broker.
subtitle: Concord's real estate market offers exceptional value compared to nearby Charlotte. With a diverse inventory ranging from historic downtown properties to modern suburban developments, buyers find options across all price points. The market has shown healthy 4.7% year-over-year appreciation, making it attractive for both first-time buyers and seasoned homeowners.

sections.heading: The Concord Housing Market
sections.html:
Popular neighborhoods include Afton Village, Centergrove, and the emerging downtown district. New construction is booming in areas like Roberta Mill and along the I-85 corridor, offering modern amenities and energy-efficient designs. Whether you're seeking a starter home, forever home, or investment property, Concord delivers quality and value.

Concord at a glance (Canopy MLS, May 2026): median sale price $360,000 · average sale price $439,299 · 43 days on market · 3.1 months of inventory.

Average Price by Home Type

Single-family homes dominate the market, offering the best value for space. New construction commands premium pricing but includes modern features and warranties.

Single-family homes dominate the market, typically running from about 1,600 to over 3,500 square feet. Townhomes and condos (roughly 1,200–1,650 sq ft) offer lower-maintenance entry points, and new construction (often 2,400+ sq ft) commands a premium for modern features and warranties. See the market reports page for current Canopy MLS pricing.

sections.heading: Popular Neighborhoods
sections.html:
Afton Village

Master-planned community with resort-style amenities, pools, and trails. Family-friendly atmosphere.

Downtown Concord

Historic homes with character, walkable to shops and restaurants. Perfect for those seeking urban lifestyle.

Centergrove

Established neighborhood with mature trees and larger lots. Strong community feel.

Roberta Mill

New construction hub with modern designs and energy efficiency. Popular with young professionals and families.

Tips for Home Buyers in Concord

  • 1

Get pre-approved:

Competitive market requires strong financing. Know your budget before house hunting.

  • 2

Consider commute:

If working in Charlotte, factor in drive times from different neighborhoods.

  • 3

Research school districts:

Cabarrus County Schools serves the area. Verify school assignments for your specific address with the district.

  • 4

Act quickly:

Well-priced homes move fast. Be ready to make offers promptly.

sections.heading: Why Buy a Home in Concord?
sections.html:
Top Reasons

  • Affordability: Median prices well below Charlotte's
  • Schools: Cabarrus County Schools district
  • Location: 25-minute commute to Charlotte Uptown
  • Growth: Steady appreciation and population growth

Market Outlook

Concord's real estate market remains strong with consistent appreciation, low inventory, and high demand. The combination of excellent schools, convenient location, and relative affordability continues to attract buyers from Charlotte and beyond.

New construction is booming in areas like Christenbury and Roberta Mill, while established neighborhoods maintain strong property values. Whether buying for appreciation potential or long-term living, Concord offers solid investment opportunities.

Franklin Bellamy, Licensed NC Real Estate Agent
